subject: Private VPC — control/data stitching and adjacency validation
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@edgegrid-solutions.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops-team@edgegrid-solutions.com
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial survey and a few adjacency questions (EdgeGrid / Redwood private VPC)

Hi Naomi & Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is the short site/network survey we promised — it highlights the existing VLAN breakdown and the peering/edge devices in our colo. A couple of items we need clarity on before we move to a formal handoff: 

- Control-plane placement: do you require a dedicated control-plane interface per tenant, or is a shared control-plane with strong ACLs acceptable for our setup?
- MTU and BFD: we saw notes in the pre-read about MTU-sensitive KV cache replication — are there hard requirements (e.g., 9000 bytes) we should enforce now?
- Hairpin/return path: we need to validate whether the onprem app firewall will hairpin traffic back into the inference cluster — this affects routing and SNAT policies on our side.

I've attached edgegrid_network_survey.pdf. If you could sketch a preferred adjacency pattern (even a rough PNG) that would make the proposal easier for procurement and colo to review.

Happy to hop on another 30m if that's easier.

—Alex
Network Architect | EdgeGrid Solutions

Attachments: edgegrid_network_survey.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@edgegrid-solutions.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial survey and a few adjacency questions (EdgeGrid / Redwood private VPC)

Thanks Alex — useful survey. I sketched a minimal adjacency pattern below and included initial constraints.

High-level (short answer):
- Control plane: we strongly prefer a logically dedicated control-plane endpoint per tenant (RFC-like separation). That can ride over a shared physical network via separate VLANs and ACLs, but from an operational and audit standpoint we want tenant control-plane interfaces isolated (separate /24s or VRF).
- Data plane: inference traffic (gRPC/tcp) can use a shared fabric with per-tenant VLAN tagging and strict egress ACLs; we rely on prefix/KV cache affinity to keep sessions sticky to a pool.
- MTU: recommend 9000 for inter-switch and host paths when using jumbo frames — this keeps KV cache streaming consistent and avoids fragmentation with large pinned payloads. If jumbo frames are not possible, we'll tolerate 1500 but will document throughput variance.
- BFD & path health: BFD on the primary transport between your edge routers and our onprem gateway is required for sub-500ms failover detection; we use BFD to trigger KV cache warmup on fallback pools.
- Hairpin: avoid hairpin where possible. If your firewall forces hairpin, we need explicit SNAT rules and a documented return path so session affinity doesn't break across the NAT.

Sketch: I've dropped an initial diagram in our Drive link (see related_links). For now, the quick adjacency model is: tenant-control-vlan -> control-plane-proxy (VRF) separate from tenant-data-vlan -> inference-svc-pool (tagged) with an edge NAT/bastion between colo and Redwood onprem gateway.

Next steps / asks:
1) Alex — can you attach a simple adjacency PNG (vpc-stitch-sketch.png) showing colo switches, edge router, firewall, and the vlan ids?
2) Marissa — FYI: if EdgeGrid can commit to MTU 9000 and BFD, we can move this to an ops preflight and schedule a dry-run.
3) Jordan & Karthik — please flag any non-starters (MTU or VRF constraints) and I'll call out any design changes.

Warm regards,
Naomi Feldman
Network Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none inline.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Alex Mercer <alex@edgegrid-solutions.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial survey and a few adjacency questions (EdgeGrid / Redwood private VPC)

Thanks Naomi — good summary. A couple of operational clarifications from infra: 

- BFD: agreed — infra requires BFD with a 300ms detect window on production paths. We'll add that to the runbook and the BFD session templates.
- MTU: if EdgeGrid can't deliver 9000, we need an explicit test matrix: 1500 vs 9000 (latency/throughput/KV cache rekey). Can you confirm if colo will allow jumbo on the leafs?
- VLAN adjacency matrix: please populate column headers in adjacency-matrix.xlsx (attached) with the expected VLAN IDs, VRF names, and a boolean column "hairpin_allowed" — that'll let procurement and colo sign off quickly.
- Observability: we need a short telemetry contract — sFlow/netflow or mirrored port to capture traffic patterns for 48hrs during the dry-run. Add this to the preflight checklist.

I'll slot a 45m dry-run on Nov 24th in case we get the MTU/BFD confirmation. If EdgeGrid needs an earlier window, propose Nov 17th and we'll triage calendar conflicts.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Platform Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: vpc-stitch-sketch.png (PNG, 48KB), adjacency-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)

Alex — appreciate the survey and the quick responses from the team. Short checklist / action items to close this out so procurement can create the SOW: 

1) EdgeGrid: confirm VLAN IDs and whether jumbo frames (9000 MTU) are enabled on the colo leafs by EOD Nov 12. Attach the final vpc-stitch-sketch.png in reply.
2) EdgeGrid: confirm whether their firewall requires hairpin/SNAT — flag "hairpin_allowed" in the adjacency spreadsheet.
3) Redwood (Jordan & Naomi): finalize the BFD template and preflight telemetry section and attach to JIRA INF-8427.
4) All: once the spreadsheet is updated, procurement will draft the SOW and we'll schedule the dry-run (Nov 17 or Nov 24 candidate windows).

If no blockers, we'll treat this as a standard private VPC attachment (no special compliance exceptions) — procurement needs the adjacency matrix and MTU answer to move forward.

I'll follow up with a brief Ops kickoff invite once the two confirmations arrive.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Deployments | Redwood Inference
